non_claims: An inventory is not an admission and not a build: a resolved source identity says nothing about whether the family builds or behaves.
The Debian Sources index is bookworm/main metadata at a pinned snapshot.  A family absent from that suite is not thereby proven absent from every Debian suite or every upstream host.
A recipe catalogue pin is repository-authored evidence, not Debian-published metadata; the two provenance kinds are recorded separately.
The four fine-grained statuses describe the unadmitted cohort.  ADMITTED_RECIPE is the complement and is not a claim that the recipe is safe, correct or complete.

source_identity_accounting.shared_sha256_note: A shared SHA-256 is recorded only when the metadata or two recipes independently name the same source archive.  No Debian-published hash is shared across two different source packages (asserted).

unresolved.note: UNRESOLVED is a result, not a placeholder.  No source URL or hash was inferred for an unresolved family.  The frozen families.json carries no upstream homepage or repository values, so those fields are UNRESOLVED for every family rather than guessed from a source package name.

vocabulary.compatibility: This inventory is additive.  It does not rewrite the runtime or build/link atlas vocabularies; their SOURCE-UNREACHABLE label is unchanged.  The four fine-grained statuses above replace that umbrella only for the unadmitted cohort, and ADMITTED_RECIPE is the complement.

ADMITTED_RECIPE.note: not part of the legacy SOURCE-UNREACHABLE bucket; these families already have a recipe

ACQUISITION_FAILED.meaning: a URL was actually tried and failed, and the failure is not evidence that the source is gone

NO_ADMITTED_RECIPE.meaning: a source identity is resolved from trusted metadata, but no admitted recipe exists yet

NO_SOURCE_MAPPING.meaning: we have not identified a trustworthy source identity; no exact Debian binary/source identity and no admitted recipe

SOURCE_UNREACHABLE_CONFIRMED.meaning: recorded evidence shows the source is demonstrably gone and the Sources index agrees
